correction.text: 'an independent principality centered on Tunis, in present-day Tunisia'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area; a 50 km circle around Tunis (7,850 km2) is the researcher's reading of 'centered on Tunis'. De facto independent but 'often recognized Zirid or Hammadid suzerainty' (to al-Nasir until 1067, then Tamim).

correction.text: Tunis and its environs, independent again after the Hammadid governors

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 1128-1147 is the Hammadid annexation ('Hammadid governors controlled Tunis until it regained independence in 1148'), for which this state has no shape. The page says Roger II of Sicily may have granted authority around this time (some historians) but not tribute; the Kingdom of Africa dossier carries a vassal reading from 1148.

region.text: Tunis and its environs, left to local leaders when al-Mu'izz moved to Mahdia in 1057

ledger.note: 1059: the people of Tunis take a Sanhaja governor and the Banu Khurasan begin. After the Banu Hilal raided Tunis and expelled its governor, the Tunisians 'asked the Hammadid emir al-Nasir for a governor' and he appointed Abd al-Haqq ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Khurasan; ruler list from 1059, infobox 'c. 1058'.

region.text: Tunis and its environs, annexed by the Hammadids

ledger.note: 1128: the Hammadids depose Ahmad and annex Tunis. 'In 1128, Ahmad was deposed and the principality was annexed to the Hammadid kingdom.'

region.text: Tunis and its environs, recovered from the Hammadids

ledger.note: 1148: Tunis is independent again. 'Hammadid governors controlled Tunis until it regained independence in 1148'; the elected qadi Abd al-Mu'min and then Abu Bakr ibn Isma'il rule that year.

1159: the Almohads end the Khurasanid rule. 'In 1159, the last Khurasanid ruler, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Aziz, was ousted by the Almohad Caliphate and sent into exile'; the Abd al-Mu'min page: he 'led his forces to conquer Tunis in 1159'.

wars.name: Zirid siege of Tunis (Tamim ibn al-Mu'izz)
wars.outcome: Abd al-Haqq recognised the Hammadid al-Nasir until 1067, then the Zirid Tamim ibn al-Mu'izz 'after a fourteen-month siege'; Tunis stayed a principality under Zirid suzerainty.
wars.note: The page gives 1067 for the change of overlord and the length of the siege, not its start year; 1066-1067 is the reading.

wars.name: Zirid siege of Tunis (1116-1117)
wars.outcome: Ahmad first recognised the Zirids, who 'besieged the city in 1116-7', then recognised the Hammadids again in 1120-1.

wars.name: Hammadid annexation of Tunis
wars.outcome: Ahmad was deposed in 1128 and Tunis annexed to the Hammadid kingdom, which held it until 1148.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of Tunis
wars.outcome: Abd al-Mu'min 'led his forces to conquer Tunis in 1159'; the last Khurasanid ruler was ousted and exiled and the Almohads annexed all of Ifriqiya.
wars.note: The Abd al-Mu'min page does not name the holder of Tunis; the Banu Khurasan page does not say who led the conquest.

certainty.note: A city principality: no page gives a frontier around Tunis.

notes: Cliopatria has no Banu Khurasan row. The principality was a city state under Zirid and Hammadid suzerainty, often recognised on paper (al-Nasir to 1067, Tamim, the Zirids again 1116-7, the Hammadids 1120-1): those overlord relations are not drawn as vassal events here, because the overlord dossiers carry them if at all. The Kingdom of Africa dossier of this group records a vassal_start in 1148 with this state as counterpart ('Banu Khurasan (Tunis)'); the Banu Khurasan page does not mention Roger II's tribute or a 1148 Norman capture of Mahdia, saying only that 'some historians suggest that Roger II of Sicily granted the Banu Khurasan authority to govern', and the Abd al-Mu'min page does not mention Tunis's holder; a reviewer should check that vassal event against the Kingdom of Africa page. Start 1059 is the ruler list and the Zirid dossier's year (infobox c. 1058). Gazetteer: Tunis resolves.
